description: Gaunt, four-horned, snow to the claws. The wings never beat. Two colours on it are wrong, and both are hot.
lore: The snow it stands in is the same colour it is, crest of the head down to the claws, so the first thing anybody sees of one is the eyes. Lean, hard, hunched forward at the shoulders. Four ivory horns off a single base, ridged like bark. Long hooked claws, grown in sets. Wings held open and never once beaten — it has had them the whole time and it comes at you on its feet. Then the specks: a rust-coloured scatter across the hide, the other wrong colour up there, since nothing that high makes rust. No fire is kept that high, no rota ever ran that far, no round goes up there at all, so there is no account of what this was to hold the thing walking around now up against. The ones found lower down can at least be argued about.

Everything on it is the colour and the temperature of the mountain, and the stone inside it is neither. Black, pebbled, a cyan vein running through it, and the vein moves. Worked into a blade it throws a spark that now and then does not stop where it lands: it carries on, from the body it found to the next body along. That mismatch is the argument about this one, and the argument is live. The people who work the high snow find no mystery in it and say so patiently — dry cold is the country that bites you when you take a glove off, and a storm is only what that gets to when there is enough of it. The people who work the stones are less easy, because a stone is supposed to be the last of what a creature was, and this creature is made of cold, and cold does not jump. What reached the bottom of it was the reaching. Past the thing in front of it, for the thing behind it.

It hunts without stopping, and there is very little up there to hunt. It moves hunched and unhurried and makes no sound on the snow, and what those claws open does not close quickly, because the cold gets into the wound and settles in. Talons drop out of it and grow back, so a patient tracker can follow one across a whole season by the sockets left in the drift behind it, ragged, always in sets. None of what it catches makes any difference. It has been starving the entire time and will go on starving, because there is nothing in there that could ever be full. When it goes down it goes all at once and stays down, and the heap darkens as it settles, and dark carries a long way up there. That is how the position gets reported at all, and the position is the trouble: a great many days uphill, on the far side of the massif from the eastern ground where this is supposed to happen, over country more of the dead have agreed on, for longer, than any other in the world. People used to call the high snow safe on exactly that reasoning, too well remembered to lose. The ones who still say it have not been up lately.
